question.text: An investor buys Nifty futures at 22,000 as a long hedge for his planned equity investment next month. On the date of investment, Nifty spot and futures have converged at 22,800. What is the effective purchase price of his investment per unit of Nifty?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 90-91), the effective purchase price for a long futures hedge equals the cash purchase cost less the gain (or plus the loss) on the futures position based on the actual futures square-off price. Step-by-step: 1. Futures bought at: Rs. 22,000 2. Futures square-off price (converged with spot): Rs. 22,800 3. Futures profit per unit = 22,800 - 22,000 = Rs. 800 4. Cash purchase cost per unit = Spot = Rs. 22,800 5. Effective purchase price = 22,800 - 800 = Rs. 22,000 The Trap: Candidates may pick the spot price (22,800) and forget to net off the futures gain, or use the futures square-off price directly as the effective price. Note: When futures and spot converge at maturity, the effective purchase price under a long hedge equals the original futures entry price, locking in the cost.
